items.titleEn: Why Nebius, CoreWeave and IREN stocks are falling after Microsoft's capex miss
items.summaryEn: Buy CoreWeave. The selloff is being driven by bond-market panic (high yields on unsecured debt) and “GPU obsolescence” fears, but Oppenheimer argues the equity is mispriced versus recoverable asset value and longer server useful lives. CoreWeave also has a software stack angle that can improve cost per MW and inference/enterprise monetization, not just raw GPU rental. Key risk: a real cash crunch—customers don’t convert AI demand into enough revenue fast enough, forcing an equity/dilution event or asset fire sale. Key Risk: CoreWeave can’t generate enough cash from AI infrastructure fast enough and must massively dilute or sell assets. Buy Nebius. It’s the cleaner balance-sheet story in the group (much lower net debt than CoreWeave) and it’s still getting incremental funding for data-center buildout (raised ~€250m). With the stock down ~23% and being priced like more leveraged peers, the risk/reward skews toward upside if financing stays available and capacity ramps in 2025. Key risk: financing conditions tighten further and the company can’t fund capex/rollouts without issuing equity at depressed prices.

items.titleEn: Tesla stock is plunging, but Elon Musk just secured a major breakthrough
items.summaryEn: Buy NASDAQ:TSLA. South Korea removes an immediate FSD refund overhang, and the article shows accelerating paid FSD adoption (active subs +67% YoY; >75% of new NA deliveries include paid FSD). That supports a shift toward recurring software revenue, which can lift margins if autonomy monetization keeps scaling. Key risk: FSD adoption keeps rising but margins don’t—operating profit and free cash flow keep deteriorating because AI/robotics spend stays ahead of monetization. Key Risk: FSD grows as a subscription but Tesla’s margins and free cash flow keep collapsing due to heavy AI/robotics spending outpacing revenue. Sell NASDAQ:TSLA short-term versus EV software peers (e.g., short TSLA vs long BYDDF/OTC:BYDDY or NIO). The court win doesn’t prove Level 5 autonomy, while the article highlights operating margin ~2.6% and operating profit down ~56% with capex still high. If the market is pricing “robotaxi profits” too early, the stock can re-rate down even after legal noise fades. Key risk: Tesla proves near-term monetization—robotaxi/FSD revenue accelerates faster than spending, forcing a valuation reset higher.

items.titleEn: How Elon Musk's SpaceX triggered an $11 billion earnings shock for Alphabet
items.summaryEn: Buy GOOGL. The $11B SpaceX hit is mostly unrealized accounting noise, while the operating engine is improving: operating profit +30% and Google Cloud revenue +103%. The market is over-penalizing a mark-to-market loss and underweighting Cloud momentum. Add on weakness from the earnings reaction. Key Risk: AI capex keeps free cash flow negative longer than expected, and search/ads growth keeps slowing so the earnings miss becomes real, not just accounting. Sell GOOG and rotate into Microsoft (MSFT) or Meta (META). Alphabet’s earnings miss is tied to rising capex and weaker search/ads, while peers are monetizing AI with less cash drain. If investors keep punishing Alphabet’s cash burn, relative performance will lag.

items.titleEn: Here's why the Kospi Index is falling after the Samsung, Google earnings
items.summaryEn: Sell KOSPI exposure (e.g., iShares MSCI South Korea ETF, EWY). Google’s weaker ad revenue and AI funding fears are hitting the same mega-cap AI supply chain that drives ~half the index. With Kospi still below the 50-day and Supertrend red, momentum favors downside toward ~5,500. Key Risk: AI sentiment flips fast and the index reclaims the 50-day (~6,400), driven by stronger-than-feared global tech earnings or renewed AI funding confidence. Sell Samsung. Even with solid operating profit, the stock fell ~5% and the market is punishing any sign that AI spending is slowing. If AI bubble fears deepen, Samsung’s valuation support from “undervalued” narratives weakens quickly because it’s the index’s biggest weight.

items.titleEn: Samsung stock plunges over 6% despite record $80B profit: here's why
items.summaryEn: Buy SK Hynix. It’s the cleaner beneficiary of the AI-memory cycle and the article highlights its shareholder-return actions alongside strong performance, which helped shares jump. Relative to Samsung, the market is rewarding Hynix for translating record earnings into confidence on future chip pricing and volumes. Key Risk: HBM demand softens or competition (especially Chinese suppliers) forces SK Hynix to cut prices, shrinking the earnings gap versus expectations. Sell Samsung Electronics. Record profit didn’t stop the drop because Device Solutions missed expectations and investors are demanding proof that AI-memory margins and pricing will hold. The stock is priced for “easy money” already, while consumer electronics is still loss-making and chip earnings expectations are rising faster than results.

items.titleEn: Marvell weighs Lumentum acquisition: upside for LITE holders, pressure for MRVL
items.summaryEn: If MRVL is weighing a Lumentum deal, LITE should trade like a takeover target: deal premium + momentum from “sold out through 2029” optics demand. Expect upside from any credible next-week announcement and from investors re-rating LITE’s growth runway (110% revenue jump this year; strong upside to estimates). Key Risk: Deal breaks or premium collapses (MRVL walks away or offers too little). MRVL is the acquirer and faces dilution + heavy financing. Paying a ~40x forward P/E for a peak-cycle asset while raising billions and issuing stock is a direct hit to near-term EPS and risk-adjusted returns. Even if the strategic logic is right, the stock reaction is typically negative until terms are proven accretive.
